newsitem.title: JAPAN: Quick Japan 'Big Bang' important - British officials.
newsitem.headline: Quick Japan 'Big Bang' important - British officials.

text.p: Speedy implementation by Japan is important in carrying out its planned comprehensive "Big Bang" reforms of financial markets, British monetary authorities told their Japanese counterparts on Monday.
"We were told that speed is very important," said a Japanese Finance Ministry official who briefed reporters after regular British-Japan financial talks held in Tokyo.

He also said British officials said it was important to set a timetable for the Big Bang reforms as that would allow financial institutions to make changes beforehand to cope with the expected reforms.

Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto has vowed to carry out an overall reform of Japanese markets to catch up by 2001 with the "Big Bang" liberalisation carried out a decade ago in Britain and with similar reforms elsewhere in Europe and in the United States.

The participants at Monday's meeting included Alan Whiting, deputy head of the British Treasury's Finance Regulation and Industry Directorate, and Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the Finance Ministry's International Finance Bureau.
The meeting has been held from time to time since 1984 and was last held in London in May 1994.

On the issue of European Monetary Union, the Japanese official quoted British participants as saying that Britain's decision on whether to take part will only be made when all the discussions are over. -- Tokyo Policy Desk (81-3-5473-3710)
